text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock barely moved today, up just 0.13%, but it's riding a strong two-week rally of 7.5% that reflects a sharp climb in oil prices. US crude is trading at $97.26 a barrel while international oil has reached $109.51—a gap driven by fresh Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and Iranian attacks in the Gulf, which have extended energy market gains. Refineries are running at 97.8% capacity, near full utilization, so the company benefits directly when crude prices rise and demand stays strong.

The broader market backdrop is adding fuel to the move: geopolitical tensions in the Middle East are proving durable, and oil and Treasury yields are now moving in lockstep at their tightest correlation since 2019, suggesting oil price swings are having outsized effects on market sentiment. For a refiner, higher crude prices can cut into margins unless they can pass costs along to customers, but the high utilization rate and global supply concerns are currently supporting the energy complex.
